title: Victoria Sandwich
description: Mrs Beeton's 1861 Victoria sandwich, an early printed version of the jam-filled butter sponge named for Queen Victoria. Beeton bakes it in one shallow tin, sandwiches the halves, and cuts it into fingers stacked in a criss-cross pile.
notes:
VICTORIA SANDWICHES.

1491. INGREDIENTS.--4 eggs; their weight in pounded sugar, butter, and flour; 1/4 saltspoonful of salt, a layer of any kind of jam or marmalade.

Mode.--Beat the butter to a cream; dredge in the flour and pounded sugar; stir these ingredients well together, and add the eggs, which should be previously thoroughly whisked. When the mixture has been well beaten for about 10 minutes, butter a Yorkshire-pudding tin, pour in the batter, and bake it in a moderate oven for 20 minutes. Let it cool, spread one half of the cake with a layer of nice preserve, place over it the other half of the cake, press the pieces slightly together, and then cut it into long finger-pieces; pile them in crossbars on a glass dish, and serve.

Time.--20 minutes.

Average cost, 1s. 3d.

Sufficient for 5 or 6 persons.

Seasonable at any time.

Isabella Beeton, *The Book of Household Management* (London, 1861), Chapter XXIX, recipe 1491, Project Gutenberg eBook #10136. Gutenberg's italic markers (underscores) are omitted.

Adapted: the weights of four eggs (about 225 g each of butter, sugar and flour) are given directly, and 2 teaspoons of baking powder are added for a reliable rise; Beeton relied on 10 minutes of beating alone.
ingredients: 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons (225 g) superfine sugar
1/2 cup (160 g) raspberry jam or marmalade
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Butter a 9-by-13-inch pan and line the bottom with parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat the butter until creamy, about 2 minutes. Add the sugar and beat until pale and fluffy, 3 to 4 minutes more.
Whisk the eggs in a separate bowl until frothy, then beat them into the butter a little at a time. Fold in the flour mixture until just combined.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan and bake until golden and springy, and a skewer comes out clean, 20 to 25 minutes.
Cool for 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely.
Cut the cake in half crosswise. Spread one half with jam, lay the other half on top, and press gently.
Trim the edges and cut into fingers about 1 inch wide. Stack them in criss-cross layers on a glass plate to serve.
